$comment: The registry of entry points that take UNTRUSTED input (a parser, a sync-frame decoder, an HTTP or MCP JSON-RPC body, a loro import, JSON across the wasm boundary, a font file), and the one list the fuzz targets are derived from (QR-28b, QR-29a). Read by `cargo xtask inputs`. Keys are `<crate>::<path to the entry function>`; `crate` repeats the key's crate and must be in crates/architecture-map.json. Each entry declares maxBytes it will read, maxDepth it will recurse or nest, maxMillis it may run, optionally maxNodes it will build, and the `fuzzTarget` in crates/fuzz that exercises it. A missing cap, a target with no entry and an entry with no target all fail. `pnpm rust:fuzz:*` runs a target with libFuzzer's -max_len at maxBytes and -timeout at maxMillis rounded up to a second. `template: true` marks the one entry that is not an untrusted-input entry: it carries the fuzz pipeline until the first ported parser lands, and its caps bound the fuzzer rather than a refusal in the function.

whiteboard-det::utf16::len.reason: template entry: a flat string, so depth 1; 4 KiB keeps libFuzzer's executions per second high, and 100 ms is far above the microseconds a 4 KiB length takes

whiteboard-wasm::spatial_edges::edge_rou.reason: the routing wire is a flat f64 array the shim builds but any holder of the wasm glue can call. maxBytes is MAX_WIRE_NUMBERS (32768) x 8, the export's own refusal: the largest corpus board's wire is 22984 bytes (clustered 12x12, 144 nodes and 165 edges), so the cap is 11.4x that; a board past it is answered by the TypeScript. maxDepth 2 is the deepest counted group (an edge's bend list inside the edge list); the decoder is iterative. maxMillis 5000 is 2.2x the slowest draw measured at the cap: 2.3 s on Node wasm for a 920-node, 2065-edge board of 251624 bytes, straight edges

whiteboard-wasm::okf::okf_parse.reason: the export reads a document's head, the fences and the frontmatter between them, so any holder of the wasm glue can call it. maxBytes is the frontmatter's own cap (frontmatter::MAX_BYTES, which whiteboard-codec::okf::parse inherits): the export refuses a head past it before reading it and the shim then answers from the TypeScript, which has no cap, so a document whose frontmatter is over 256 KiB takes the TypeScript's path. The body is not in the head: the shim cuts the head at the closing fence and keeps the body, so a body of any size is read and its size is no input to this cap (a UTF-16 length is never over its UTF-8 one, so the shim's own check on the head refuses nothing the export would take). A lone surrogate in the head crosses as a mark the host chooses, which the export looks for among the strings and keys it read. maxDepth 64 is the YAML reader's MAX_PARSE_DEPTH, the deepest it recurses; the answer is built by one walk of what it produced and adds no nesting beyond one array per mapping or list. maxMillis 500 is 6.5x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm, 77 ms for a 262129-byte frontmatter holding a flow list of ~131k integers (the others at the cap took under 50 ms: 49 ms for a type that is a mapping with a 130k-item length list, 43 ms for 23k integer keys, 34 ms for 22k preserved keys, 23 ms for 2.5k trust events with extra keys, 15 ms for 43k tags, 6 ms for a 262k scalar, double-quoted or block); the codec's own 250 ms is native, this one carries the wire on wasm

whiteboard-wasm::okf::okf_serialize.reason: the export reads the wire of a frontmatter (JSON in the value wire of okf_wire.rs), so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. maxBytes 262144 is the parse entry's: a frontmatter the reader would take is within it as YAML, and the wire is a little larger than the YAML it spells (a double is 22 bytes of wire where its YAML is as short as one), so a frontmatter near the reader's cap is answered by the TypeScript. A wire past it is refused before it is parsed. maxDepth 64 is the writer's nesting cap (MAX_PARSE_DEPTH): a deeper value answers unwritable, and serde_json's own 128-level recursion limit (deny.toml bans unbounded_depth) sits above it because the wire spends one array level per mapping or list. maxMillis 250 is 8.8x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm, 28 ms for 18.5k integer-like keys under facetsRaw (the canonical order sorts them and JavaScript's enumeration puts them first); 20 ms for 2.6k trust events with extra keys, 14 ms for 12k facet keys, 8 ms for a 224 KiB string of escapes, 7 ms for 11k numbers and 5 ms for a 262k string. A search of the held keys for each preserved key had made a 16k-key record 147 ms, and quadratic; the writer indexes them now. A refusal names every place a value has no spelling and each place repeats its whole path, so the walk stops once the faults weigh MAX_FAULT_BYTES (1 MiB: the keys of each path, 8 bytes a step and 32 a fault) and the export answers input-too-large. Unbounded, 60 nested 1000-byte keys over 5000 NaN leaves in a 185 KB wire answered 301 MB in 4.6 s and 1.3 GB of resident memory on Node wasm; bounded, the same wire is refused in 15-19 ms at 63 MB. Within the budget the slowest answer measured is 18 ms for 3000 NaN leaves under 20 keys (a 548 KB answer), and 12 ms for 2000 (365 KB); 6000 NaN keys and 8000 keys holding a byte-order mark took 9 ms each

whiteboard-codec::frontmatter::parse.reason: the OKF frontmatter YAML reader takes the text between a document's fences, from a file, an import or a sync, so any holder of a document can call it. maxBytes is MAX_BYTES, the function's own refusal (a longer text answers TooLarge before it is read): frontmatter is metadata, and the largest the repository carries is a few kilobytes, so the cap is far above any document and bounds the fuzzer's cost. maxDepth 64 is MAX_PARSE_DEPTH: past MAX_DEPTH (32) the visit refuses, and the parse recurses to 64 only so that a document malformed further down is named malformed first; deeper is refused outright. maxMillis 250 is 13x the slowest draw measured at the cap: 18.9 ms natively in release for a 262144-byte flow sequence of 131067 items (the 24 other shapes tried, among them one long scalar, many short keys, long block and quoted scalars, a 256 KiB hex literal and an alias flood, took under 14 ms)

whiteboard-codec::okf::parse.reason: the OKF envelope reads a whole document from a file, an import or a sync, so any holder of one can call it. maxBytes is the frontmatter's own cap (frontmatter::MAX_BYTES), the refusal parse inherits: the text between the fences is read only up to it, and past it the answer is a YAML refusal. The body is not read at all: the closing-fence search scans it once and it is copied once, so it is not capped (the TypeScript has no cap either) and fuzzing at the frontmatter's cap covers the shapes that cost. maxDepth 64 is MAX_PARSE_DEPTH, the deepest the YAML reader recurses; the schema and the key reordering walk what it produced and add no nesting. maxMillis 250 is 5.6x the slowest draw measured natively in release: 44.4 ms for a frontmatter of 262101 bytes whose type is a mapping with a 131050-item length list (the schema renders it to a string to measure it). The other shapes tried at the cap took 7 to 28 ms (a flow list, 26k preserved keys, 26k integer keys that JavaScript enumerates first, 26k refused facet keys, 6k trust events with extra keys, 26k tags), and a 16 MiB body took 4.4 ms, 15.7 MiB of near-miss fences 19 ms and 21 MiB of CRLF near-misses 26 ms

whiteboard-codec::json_canvas::parse.reason: the JSON Canvas reader takes a whole board from a file, an import, a paste or a sync, so any holder of one can call it. maxBytes is json_canvas::MAX_BYTES, the function's own refusal (a longer text answers Declined(TooLarge) before it is read, and the caller asks the TypeScript, which has no cap): a board of a few thousand nodes is a few hundred kilobytes, so 4 MiB is far above any board and bounds the fuzzer's cost. maxDepth 64 is json::MAX_DEPTH: the document nests six levels deep before a facet payload begins, and a text nested past 64 answers Declined(TooDeep) the moment the 65th level opens, whatever follows it. maxMillis 2000 is 2.6x the slowest draw measured natively in release: 773 ms for a 4 MiB text of 270k integer-like keys in one facet payload (the reader builds the tree, then puts JavaScript's enumeration order on every object). The other shapes tried at the cap took 10 to 717 ms (a payload of wide arrays nested 55 deep 717, 270k keys at the root 258, 270k facet keys 189, a node list 98 to 111, an edge list refused for its ends 142, a list of invalid nodes 494, a 4 MiB string 11), and a node list written back took 98 to 144 ms in the extended and strict modes

whiteboard-wasm::json_canvas::json_canva.reason: the export reads a whole board's text, so any holder of the wasm glue can call it. maxBytes and maxDepth are whiteboard_codec::json_canvas's own (MAX_BYTES, MAX_DEPTH): the export refuses a text past the first before reading it and the shim then answers from the TypeScript, which has no cap, and a text nested past the second answers a decline the same way. maxMillis 3000 is 2.6x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm, 1146 ms for a 3.82 MiB list of nodes the schema refuses (the others at the cap took 24 to 738 ms: 738 for 270k integer-like keys in one facet payload, 598 for facet keys at the root, 569 for wide arrays nested 55 deep, 544 for 3.84 MiB of valid text nodes, 498 for edges refused for their ends, 24 for one 4 MiB string); the codec's own 2000 is native, this one carries the answer's wire on wasm.

the export reads the wire of a canvas (JSON in the value wire of json_canvas_wire.rs), so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. maxBytes is the parse entry's, so a canvas the reader would take is within it as text; the wire of a canvas is about 18% bigger than the text written from it, so a board whose text is over about 3.4 MiB is past the cap and is answered by the TypeScript, and a wire past it is refused before it is parsed. maxDepth 128 is serde_json's own recursion limit (deny.toml bans unbounded_depth), which one array per object or list spends one level of each; the writer's cap is the same, and the shim sends nothing past 100. maxMillis 1000 is 2.9x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm, 344 ms for a canvas holding 250k integer-like facet keys (the extended mode; the others took 80 to 309 ms: 309 for the 11,000-node board in the strict mode, 221 extended, 212 for 120k facet keys at the root, 197 for 150k nested lists, 107 for 300k tags)
